chunk_findings.detail: The new standing-wait branch prints `w['holder']` in the slot that names the entity that “has waited”. In this schema `w['holder']` is the item holding the files, not the waiting item: `_overtaken_waiters` keys `blocked_before` by `w.item`, and `WG.waiting_for(st, cfg, iid, now)` selects waits for held item `iid` where `w.holder == iid`. Therefore for held item `H` and standing waiter `W`, the brief renders `H has waited for the files H holds (for W)`, which is backwards. It should print `w['item']`, not `w['holder']`, so `test_the_brief_names_the_overtaken_waiter` will fail any case where the holder and waiter differ.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/brief.py:_waiting_on_you

chunk_findings.detail: The overtake note is built only after `L.retarget`, and the emitted name is `w.holder`. The bug being fixed is that a standing wait’s holder pointer moves to the agent that just widened, so `WG.waiters` then reports that new holder, not the waiter. Given DX-wait-cycle-followups widening onto `ddflow/api/lifecycle/` while B-hy-stop-protocol has a standing wait on that prefix, the reply becomes `overtook: DX-wait-cycle-followups (B-hy-stop-protocol)` (or whatever id now holds the lease) instead of naming the overtaken waiter, so the silence defect is replaced by the wrong party.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/items/_edit.py:_overtaken_waiters

chunk_findings.detail: The new brief line treats `w['holder']` as the agent who has been waiting, but that field is the blocker the wait points at. After the same widen, a brief for the new holder reads as if that holder “has waited … for the files” the holder itself holds, and the standing waiter is only a parenthetical `(for …)`. That does not tell the holder who it overtook.

chunk_findings.detail: The negative case forbids the behavior the bug requires. DX already holds `ddflow/api/lifecycle/brief.py`, BHY's refused update leaves a standing wait on `ddflow/api/lifecycle/`, then DX runs `update --globs ddflow/api/lifecycle/` and the test asserts `"overtook" not in out`. That update grants the directory glob the standing wait asks for, including paths under `lifecycle/` DX did not already hold, which is the silent-overtake the intent says the reply must name. A correct fix that prints the overtaken waiter (`bhy` / `BHY`) on that grant fails this test, so the regression locks the defect in for a directory widen over a file the same agent already held.

chunk_findings.detail: Still holds. The added `and not diff_is_trivial(it, cfg, repo, paths)` is still evaluated before the existing `repo is not None` guard on the next line. In the function's `repo is None` path for a non-doc task, Python reaches this new expression first and calls `diff_is_trivial` with `repo=None`; `diff_is_trivial` inspects the git worktree/diff to compare ASTs, so it fails on `None` before the existing guard can take the intended branch. The triage note “code rewritten” does not answer this finding: the cited call site is unchanged, and it still orders a repo-dependent call ahead of the only `repo is None` handling in the chain.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/completion/rules.py:233

chunk_findings.detail: The classifier only compares the first token of `git ls-tree` output, so a symbolic link (`120000`) is still treated like a regular `.py` source file. `_show` then returns the symlink *target text* via `git show`, and `_py_ast_equal` parses that target text as Python. A committed change that retargets `foo.py` from `a.py` to `(a).py` has mode `120000` at both refs; the blobs are `a.py` and `(a).py`, which produce identical ASTs because parentheses are not represented in the AST, and `_shebang()` is `b""` for both. `_ast_unchanged` therefore returns `True`, and `diff_is_trivial` returns `True`, even though `import foo` now loads a different file (`(a).py` instead of `a.py`), a behavior-changing change. Non-regular object types such as `120000` (symlink) or `160000` (gitlink) must fail closed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/docsonly.py:_ast_unchanged

chunk_findings.detail: `_py_ast_equal` claims a file that does not parse fails closed, but the `except` list omits `UnicodeDecodeError`. `ast.parse` on raw bytes decodes as UTF-8 when there is no PEP 263 cookie, and invalid UTF-8 raises `UnicodeDecodeError` (not `SyntaxError`/`ValueError`/`TypeError`/`MemoryError`). Given `a.py` whose committed bytes are `s = "` plus `0xE9` plus `"` (latin-1, no coding cookie) at `base` and the same file with a comment-only edit at `HEAD`, `_show` returns those bytes, `_py_ast_equal` raises, and `diff_is_trivial` aborts gate selection instead of returning false and keeping full review+ci.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/docsonly.py:84

data.probe: diff_is_trivial returns False when repo is None (its guard 'if not paths or repo is None: return False' short-circuits BEFORE any git worktree inspection), so a non-doc repo=None verdict never inspects git; no crash possible

chunk_findings.detail: The new standing-wait line treats `w['holder']` as the waiting item, but standing wait records carry the waiting item in `item` and the holding item in `holder`; this same change’s `_overtaken_waiters` uses `w.item` as the overtaken waiter identity and returns `"item": w.item` for exactly that purpose. In the trigger scenario where `DX-wait-cycle-followups` is the new holder and `B-hy-stop-protocol` is the standing waiter, the brief line for `iid = DX-wait-cycle-followups` would render something like “- DX-wait-cycle-followups has waited … for the files DX-wait-cycle-followups holds (for B-hy-stop-protocol)”, failing to name the actual waiter and still misreporting the overtake the fix must surface.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/brief.py:_waiting_on_you

chunk_findings.detail: The added `if data.get("globs_overtook"):` block is indented 8 spaces, putting it inside the body of the preceding `if data.get("globs_dropped"):` block; the following `for name in ("needs", "tags"):` is at 4 spaces, so the overtook branch is not a sibling of the dropped-globs branch. In the exact reported scenario the update overtakes a standing wait but does not drop a live-lease glob, so `globs_dropped` is absent/empty and this block is never evaluated; the reply still omits the overtaken-waiter note, leaving the original silence defect unfixed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/update_message.py:26

chunk_findings.detail: The test asserts that after BHY has a standing wait on `ddflow/api/lifecycle/`, updating DX from `ddflow/api/lifecycle/brief.py` to `ddflow/api/lifecycle/` should **not** produce an `overtook` message. That contradicts the fix’s own definition: an update that grants DX exactly the glob BHY’s standing wait already asks for (`ddflow/api/lifecycle/`) is an overtake, even if DX previously held a contained file. Before this update, no agent held the directory glob BHY was waiting for; after it, the wait points at the new holder of that exact glob. A correct implementation would say `overtook`, so this test would reject a correct fix, while an implementation that silently missed this overtake would pass.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_brief_standing_wait_names_overtaken.py:test_a_wider_glob_that_only_subsume_a_held_file_is_not_an_overtake

chunk_findings.detail: `test_a_wider_glob_that_only_subsume_a_held_file_is_not_an_overtake` locks in the silence this bug is supposed to remove. DX starts holding only `ddflow/api/lifecycle/brief.py`; BHY’s refused update leaves a standing wait on `ddflow/api/lifecycle/`; DX then runs `update DX --globs ddflow/api/lifecycle/`, which replaces that single file with the directory glob BHY is waiting on (every other path under `lifecycle/`, not a restatement of `brief.py`). The bug requires that reply to name the overtaken waiter; the test asserts `"overtook" not in out`, so a correct note fails the suite and a silent grant of the waited-for glob still passes.
